Most of the girls are staying at the step no.2 and 3 of our village. Because our village girls can take some small decisions of their life, but they can’t take any important decisions as the village women cannot take part in making decisions about family matters.

Men of village don’t give any chance to women about family matters. They think that their decisions are always right. So, women’s opinions aren’t needed. A girl may take a decision about her education but she can never take about her marriage at all. When parents think that their girl should be married then they choose a bridegroom as their wish without any opinion whether she wants to study more or she is ready for marriage or not. For this reasons, we think that most of our village girls are in the steps 2 and 3.

The women of those families can take their decisions about all important matters whose husbands are either in abroad or passed away and widows are to do all the family works because most of the cases they don’t have any reliable person to give suggestions. so, for this reasons they are in the step of 4 and 5 but such kind women are few in the village.

We think that education is the undeniable needs for every person. To get education, it is necessary to go to school for every children. Without education we cannot maintain a better livelihood in the future. For leading standard life, education must be needed.
I think man is blind except education and without having education s/he has not any knowledge. So, s/he cannot understand many things about life.

I have been married in my early age. That is why I couldn’t study more but now I can realize that how much important education is to walk on the path of life. For not having education, I’m to face many problems. Now I feel that if I had a certificate of SSC then I’d get a small job which could bear more expenses of my family.
We think that education is the most essential among the basic human needs. If we have education we can manage our other needs.
Generally, Our village boys read up to class ten then they are involved with works for supporting family [All the participants are agreed].
Most of the boys give up getting education for not perceiving the importance of this and parents are not sincere about making their boys lettered.

Besides these, many parents are unable to bear the expenses of their boys’ education and further reason is not having any interest to study in the village boys. Numerous boys go abroad to work every year from our village. There is no way for a boy that after taking higher studies, he can do a better job because to get a job he is to give about 7/8 lakhs TK. But if he goes abroad by investing half of this money, he can earn more by not wasting money on education. So, parents of this village are interested to send their boys abroad than to make them educated.
Another reason is that to get a job is the matter of luck. They may get or not. So, avoiding these risks, parents send their boys abroad as if they can earn more money to adorn the future.

At present, the girls of our village are more advanced than the boys. The girls are more successful in passing SSC (Secondary School Certificate) in comparative to the boys. In our village, 5 girls are studying in college out of 10 accomplishing their SSC (Secondary School Certificate). And the rest are getting married before sitting for SSC examination. Considering these situations, we can say that most of the girls study up to class ten before marriage as if they are in the age of marriage. To avoid the early marriage (otherwise they may face legal complexities), parents are to wait till their marriage age. And if any girl can pass the SSC, she gets married with a better bridegroom. So, girls’ literacy rate is high than the boys in our village.

We think a boy should complete his masters degree and finishing his study he should take a job by dint of own capacity. If the boys are literate, the village will be more developed and then literacy rate and consciousness about the environment of village will be increased.
On the other hand, a girl should pass the SSC at least because they don’t need to take any job. So, if they study up to ten, they can teach their child.

And boys if they complete their MS (Masters), they can get a better career. After that, they can live a standard life and maintain the family expenses. As a boy can’t get any job without having MS (Masters), he should pass the MS at least.

At the present time, the parents of our village give more importance on girls’ education. Because they think that if a girl can be learned enough, she’ll get married in a good family. In such way, their girls will be happy. Another thing in our village is that parents want to make them studious but they (boys and girls) don’t want to study. Boys are busy with mobile phone and girls are busy with TV (television). Their valuable times are wasted by these devices. Though their parents want to continue till class ten they think they are educated more than their parents. Thus they are dropped out.
Now, Parents are more sincere about girls’ education than boys as if girls can manage the behavior with the people of husband’s family. Because educated girls know how to show good manner.
The girls of our village don’t do any work in the field. Boys work in the field and girls perform their household chores.

The girls learn how to cook, how to cultivate vegetables like gourd, pumpkin, tomato, watercress, spinach, bean and so on in the yard from their childhood. As we are born in farmers’ family, we are to learn these works to help their parents.
As from childhood we observe how our parents work, thus we learn to cultivate or to do others household chores and we don’t need any training.

They learn how to thrash the paddy, wheat, corn and so forth. After cutting the wheat, it is carried to home and girls thrash the wheat and chuff is differentiated by puffing from wheat. Then wheat is dried in the sun and after that we store the wheat carefully as seed.

The girls also pare of wheat after bringing from the field and dry in the sun. Even they desiccate jute, boil and desiccate the paddy, thrash the pea. These are the works for the village girls. They learn these from their mothers.
Reasons for ending education

There are many reasons for ending education but the principal reason is worse economic condition of parents. That’s why they cannot study more. If I say about myself, my parents couldn’t bear expenses of study for poverty and arranged my early-age marriage.

One thing is very important for not taking enough education is that getting married in the early age. If parents get any boon when a girl in class 8, 9 or 10, they arrange her marriage. Though her wish is to continue the study, she can’t do that for getting married.

Most of the husbands promise that if she has any wish to study, she can but after that parents of husband, husband including his brothers-sisters say that it is not needed to continue study after marriage as she won’t do any job. Thus she can’t study anymore.
Many people say that what the benefits are by making them educated. By getting married she has to go to another family. Thinking like this they prefer to search a groom for their girls.

They choose a boy who has his own house, huge money, 6/7 bighas land but they don’t want to verify his character whether he belongs good nature or not. The village people think that as the groom has enough money and land, his future will be good and their daughters will be happy.

Another reason of ending education of the girls is that the men of this village think that if the girls are more educated, they won’t listen to them (men), they will be cleverer and so on. So, they (men) say “They should be controlled by men” because they are not agreed to give the control in women’s hand. So they don’t give any importance on female education.

In the last year, there many new ideas and technological practices have been started. One year ago, there has been brought a “SEEDER” machine in this village. By this Machine, people can plant seed in the land by line and in this system there is not needed traditional earlier cultivation. For thrashing wheat, there has been an auto machine for five years in our village which can thrash the crops in short time.

In the previous years, there was not arranged any training about agriculture. But now different kinds of training about new innovation and technological are provided. Brother XX and the Upazilla Agricultural officer have begun a field-day by observing for one year in our village. This day is observed near 3 or 4 times in a year. Here, they discuss many things about agriculture whether there is any new idea or innovation and new technology which can boost the cultivation for more production of crops. The village people can present here for learning how to use a machine, how to prevent the insects and so many things related farming. In this field-day discussion, many people come from other villages to listen.

At present, there are many kinds of new seeds in our village, for which crops production has been increased. A few years ago, the village people used the domestic seeds but now most of them are using hybrid seeds. The new seeds are “prodip” 21 gama (wheat)” satabdi gama (wheat)” . We know about these new seeds from the field-day discussion.

1. We think for women, the auto thresher machine of wheat and paddy is the most important here. [7/8 FGD participants are agreed]. Because, women were used to threshing paddy and wheat by hand in the past and at that time, after cutting the crops at first they needed to dry the crops for 7/8 days and then they threshing by hand when they had to work hard or suffer more. Now it is not necessary to dry before threshing by auto thresher machine. After cutting the crop, it is easy to thresh by the auto machine immediately.
Now the people can thresh their crops in a day instead of 7/8 days. So, for these reasons, the auto thresher machine is very important for women.
2. The second most important agricultural practice for women is the “field-day”.

Because, the village women can know and learn many things about agriculture from this day’s discussion which knowledge they didn’t know in the past. They present here with their husbands and can discuss with them (Hubbies) for knowing important information.

A woman can cultivate if her husband is no more. Because she can know everything what she needs to farm by joining there without her husband. And she can recruit some laborer for farming or by suggesting her sons if she has.
Our village people are getting unbelievable efficacy in the production of wheat by using the SEEDER machine and they knew about it from the field-day program for the first time.
So, We can say that the “field-day” is the most important for the women of our village.
(Opposite sex of FGD) The two important practices for Male:

“SEEDER machine” is the most important practices for Male. Because, they planted seeds by hand in the past but now they can plant seeds by using the seeder machine without any extra earlier cultivation and for this reason time, cost and labor are being saved than the past. Besides these, people can farm jute using this machine.

Another important agricultural practice for men is “new hybrid seeds”. The men of our village are producing more crops by planting this hybrid seeds than the past. They are producing about 40 maund wheat using hybrid seeds in one bigha land where they produced 20 maund wheat by using domestic seeds. Because, the hybrid seeds are heavy and have more weight. Accordingly, the farmers are being economically benefited and poverty is being decreased.

The girls of our village don’t get enough opportunities to try out the new practices, technologies, knowledge and information about agriculture like the boys. Because, they don’t work in the field and they are prohibited to work in the field by men.
To work in the field is very bad for a girl’s family and also for her in our village. So, they don’t work in the field.

Even if, they can’t join in the field-day program where men, women and boys can join then they might miss something. Many of them said that, “what they will do by knowing everything! Will she feed us? You don’t need to know many things”.

Important wheat innovation for women Now
• 1.The auto thresher machine for wheat
• There has been auto thresher machine of wheat; women can do their works easily. At the present time, wheat can be threshed in a day by low labor where there 7/8 days were needed to thresh all the wheat in the past.
• 2.The seeder machine
• The seeder machine can cultivate land and plant the seeds at the same time that is why women don’t need to go to the field. As the seeder machine does such work in short time, women are not to do many works. A woman can farm wheat easily by seeder machine.
• 3.The field-day
• The women of our village have known farming procedures of wheat because of having this training.

Important wheat innovation for women Ten years ago
• 1. Ten years ago, people ploughed their land by using plough and then they spattered the seeds. Thus they cultivated wheat.
• 2. At that time, there were power tiller, tractor and plough to cultivate the land.
• In that period, firstly, land was framed by the plough and then was raked by ladder. Then after, seeds were spattered in the land. Again that was raked by ladder as if the seeds were mixed with the land for protecting from birds and other animals.
• 3. Before, there was thresher and to thresh the wheat they had to wait for3 or 4 days to dry the crops then they could thresh wheat. In the past, wheat was grind by the grinder.

There has been changed many things in agriculture of our village by past ten years such as there has been begun to use the auto thresher machine instead of thresher machine. For having more advancement in the auto thresher, people are using this more than earlier thresher machine.

Before, there was thresher and to thresh the wheat they had to wait for3 or 4 days to dry the crops then they could thresh wheat. But in new auto thresher machine wheat can be threshed immediately. As a result, time is saved.

Now, very few people of our village cultivate their land by plough for producing wheat. Most of our village people farm their land by power tiller, tractor. Till today, all people didn’t begin to cultivate by using the seeder machine properly.

Before ten years, they prepared the seeds according to local method. But in this time, they collect (buy) the hybrid seeds from the field-day program and then cultivate. Ten years earlier, people grinded the wheat in the grinder. But now there are some mills to grind the wheat in our locality. We make flour grinding the wheat from these mills.

These changes have been possible only because of this digital age. The transportation system has been developed by the passage of time and for good communication with the town, technological changes are spreading out across our village and people are getting more advantages.

The male and female youths of our village follow the traditional customs to do agricultural works which are defined for male and female separately. In this village, female do the household chores and male do the field works. We followed this custom from our childhood. So, Male youth and female do their distributed works. Basically, female help the male when they bring the crops from the field. These are the customs of our village.

A male youth, if he wants to sell his crops (Wheat or Rice) in the market after producing by own capacity, he can do that. He won’t face any problem because, the young male member and old male member sell their crops (wheat and rice) in the local market.

A young woman can not try to produce crops (wheat and rice) for having social restrictions in our village that is why she cannot cultivate the land by own and cannot sell the crops in the market. Because, it is considered as an ignoble when she goes to the market for selling crops. It is also an embarrassing for her family as well as her relatives.
In our village, women have enough honors that are why society doesn’t allow women to go to the market.
Men also prohibit their women as they bring all daily needs from market even what women need. But those women go to the market once within many days and buy all necessary products who are widow.

Another thing is that women need not to go to the market because if they want they can sell vegetables to the village families. Hawkers don’t come to our village to sell vegetables that’s why we are to buy or sell vegetables among ourselves. Though it is not possible to get the price like XX market, sometimes they get proper price like the market for green vegetables.
There is no matter that some land is distributed for specific family and another for another family. The male member of a family is the owner of the land in our village.
Though most of the people have their own land, someone can mortgage land from others and cultivate.
It is not applicable for Bangladesh
When there is a season of cultivation for specific crop, all the members take part in this job.
There is no fixed work for anyone. There is no rule for the distribution of work.
Generally, when a woman try out new kind of agricultural practices, she takes her husband’s suggestions because, without his concern, it is not possible to try out new practices or anything else.
On the contrary, when a man tries out new agricultural practices, he takes suggestions from agricultural officer and discuss with his wife about new practices.

A young girl cannot move to the market in our village because if she goes to market except any companion, people will reproach her. For the fear of criticism, girls don’t want to go market alone.
Another thing is that if a young girl goes to the market alone, the numerous male people stare at her which is embarrassing so much that’s why girls don’t want to go to market.

A young woman is supervised by natal families before her marriage and those responsibilities shifted to husband and his family after marriage. Later she has to depend on her husband’s decision although this is not commonly occurred here.

After marriage, they don’t go to local market. Cause there is many customs for her as a daughter in law. If she goes to market then it will be ignoble for her husband’s family and the villagers will condemn.

After marriage, she cannot go either with her cousin or sister-in-law’s husband. If she goes with them, there may begin a new illegal love-affair with them. So, there is a restriction to company with them.
If she wants to go to market, she can go with her husband, Father-in-law, brother and her parents.

It is seen in our village that a girl is married at the age of 15 and boys are marrying at the age of `18. After coming together, they begin their own family.
Generally parents decide about marriage of their sons and daughters.

The parents begin to search a bridegroom for a girl when she is in the age of 14. The matchmakers of our village talk to the parents if they see any girl of 14 years and say that, “there is a good groom, and you can arrange the marriage for your girl”. Then getting the consent of them the match-maker begins to communicate between the two families and thus they arrange a marriage without any consent of the girl whether she is ready for getting married or not. Afterwards, she gets married with the groom who is chosen by her parents.

If any girl doesn’t want to be married, parents convince the groom’s family members by saying that girl is not enough mature so she cannot understand but she will be right after some days going your family. This same thing is also happened to the boys where boys’ consent is avoided. So, a boy has to marry according to their parents.
We think that marriage should be arranged after taking the consent of girls and boys.
We also think that it is good to marry one according to their quality, status etc e.g. if a girl’s age is 18, her parents should arrange a marriage according to her consent.
On the other hand, parents should give the freedom to the boy to marry a girl after doing good job according to his desire.

And Parents should listen to their children whether they are ready for marriage or not before arranging the marriage, whether they want to get married with the bride or groom who is liked by their parents. If both of girl and boy comply with each other than marriage should be arranged.

After getting married, women take their first child within 1 or 2 years. It implies that if a girl get married in the age of 15, her first child is born at the age of 16 or 17. But most of cases, the age is 16.

We think that 16 or 17 is not suitable time to get the first child for the girls because, to get the baby in this age is very risky for girl health. At the time of bearing the child both of them are in risk even they may die.
For having a baby, girls’ health is not mature enough at the age of 16. As a result, mother’s health may face harm as well as the baby cannot be healthy and may face malnutrition.
We think that girls should be married at least in the age of 18 and they should take their first child at age of 20 so that the girls’ health is not in any risk for baby getting enough nutrition.
The age 20 is suitable time for taking a baby as if the baby will be healthy. To rear a baby, girls need enough physical and mental growth.

In our village husbands take decision for having child in the most cases. The women cannot decide alone most of the time. There has some influence of husband’s parents and others. Sometimes, mother-in-law suggests having a baby.
